findings.summary: nix::sys::wait::waitid is cfg-gated off Apple targets entirely (contract claimed it safe with zero new unsafe); libc::waitid IS declared for Apple, so the confirmed P6-4 gap is one safe wrapper function (one unsafe block), not a from-scratch extern block

bugsFoundAndFixedDuringThisExperiment.summary: waitid_probe omitted WNOHANG, causing it to block the calling thread until the target PID actually exited -- hung Reaper::register on any not-yet-exited child, and stalled the shared reaper thread's periodic sweep for every other PID
bugsFoundAndFixedDuringThisExperiment.diagnosedVia: live process observed at near-zero parent CPU with a spinning unterminated child ~4.75 minutes after test start, found via ps/lsof, not a harness-reported hang
bugsFoundAndFixedDuringThisExperiment.fix: add libc::WNOHANG to the waitid flags

bugsFoundAndFixedDuringThisExperiment.summary: the registration-time direct probe and the background sweep's probe could race on the same PID; the loser saw ECHILD (a same-reaper double-reap artifact, not a genuine sole-owner violation) -- caused a spurious ~25% Lost-outcome rate in the soak before the fix

eP6_3AdversarialStreamNoDeadlockBoundedM.matrixRowsNotAttemptedReason: require the real control-protocol shape (control_request/control_response, can_use_tool), which needs the P6-3 codec; no codec was built to service this experiment either, matching E-P6-1's scope discipline
